stem.en: A tall pea plant is crossed with a short one, and the children are half tall, half short. Kabir says "that breaks three to one". What were the parents?

text.en: The tall parent was a hybrid, Tt, not pure. Tt crossed with tt gives two boxes Tt, tall, and two boxes tt, short: one to one. The ratio tells you the hidden factor was there.

feedback.en: Half and half is exactly what the square predicts for Tt crossed with tt. The rule holds; the tall parent was not pure.

text.en: Short is dominant in this variety.

feedback.en: If short were dominant, a pure tall crossed with any short would give all short. Half and half means a hybrid parent.

text.en: The children got factors from only one parent.

feedback.en: Every child got one from each. The square with Tt and tt gives one to one.

explanation.en: Work backward from the ratio. One to one means one parent was a hybrid, the other pure recessive. This is the test cross Mendel used to check a plant's hidden factors.
